chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام:
"That Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment regarding the fetus of a Jewish, Christian, and Magian woman: [its compensation is] one-tenth of the blood-money of its mother."

key_terms.أُمِّهِ: his mother; meaning the mother of the fetus, whose diyah is the basis of calculation
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ: a Christian woman; included in the same legal ruling
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيَّةِ: a Magian woman; likewise included in the ruling
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيَّةِ: a Jewish woman; here, the mother whose fetus is under discussion
key_terms.جَنِينِ: fetus; the unborn child for whom legal compensation is being determined
key_terms.دِيَةِ: blood-money; the legally prescribed financial compensation
key_terms.عُشْرَ: one-tenth; the specified fractional amount of compensation
key_terms.قَضَى: gave judgment; issued a formal legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for the fetus of a Jewish, Christian, or Magian woman according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal judgment from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning compensation for the loss of a fetus carried by a non-Muslim woman from the protected communities mentioned. It establishes that the indemnity for such a fetus is one-tenth of the mother's diyah, reflecting a specific ruling within the law of bodily injury and compensation.
